prize_parts.citation: For the development of ligand-controlled palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: B030 for Buchwald and Hartwig and B058 for Liu. B030 is the part I can defend on structural and mechanistic evidence. The decisive step was a ligand concept, bulky electron-rich phosphines that make oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination proceed for a very wide range of amines and aryl halides. That mechanism was worked out by isolating and characterising the palladium intermediates, not only by scope tables, and the method has been used independently for about three decades in pharmaceutical, process and materials chemistry. B058 is the one achievement on the shortlist that most of the room already includes, and no one has argued it is scientifically unsound. It is an engineered deaminase tethered to a programmable DNA-binding protein, with directed evolution creating the adenine deaminase, so the novelty is molecular design of a protein-based reagent and not cleavage biology. I weighed again whether to drop to a single part, but each part holds up on its own. The two parts are scientifically unrelated, and I would present them openly as two distinct achievements rather than as one theme. Two parts with three names stay within the limit.
statement.case_against: The main weakness is still that the two parts do not belong together, and a two-part prize is justified only if each part is independently strong. B030 had only two opening supporters and the 2010 cross-coupling prize may make it look like an extension to some members. B058 is about ten years old with a short clinical record and follows the 2020 CRISPR prize closely. Naming Liu alone excludes Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida, and naming Buchwald and Hartwig leaves out Kosugi as a precursor. These are real attribution costs that I accept only because of the three-person limit. If the committee decides base editing needs Komor and Gaudelli, I would sooner pair Liu with fewer other names than abandon either part, but I recognise that would break my configuration.

responses.point: Somfai holds the same B030 plus B058 configuration and argues that C-N coupling needed a new ligand concept and a separate mechanism, with Kosugi's tin-amide work as a precursor, while he admits the committee may see it as an extension of the 2010 prize.
responses.response: We agree on laureates and on the main risk, and I take the chair's question on Kosugi seriously. The evidence I would put forward is that Kosugi's tin-amide reaction was stoichiometric in tin and limited in scope, and that the general catalytic amination of aryl halides with free amines and a base, using designed ligands and with mechanistic proof, came from Buchwald and Hartwig. That supports a citation worded around ligand-controlled catalysis and not around the first C-N coupling event, and I would word it that way so the Kosugi priority is acknowledged in the background. I do not share your view that the pairing is merely tolerable because colleagues rank B058 highly. I think B058 must stand on its own chemical argument, and I give it in the case above.

responses.point: Aqvist, who ranked B058 first, argues for Liu alone on the grounds that Liu conceived and led the programme, while he concedes that Kondo and Nishida's independent Target-AID work and the first experiments by Komor and Gaudelli split the committee.
responses.response: I agree with Liu alone and with his candid statement of the cost. Round 1 left my own position slightly inconsistent, so let me be exact. I still think Komor and Gaudelli did the decisive first experiments, and it would be wrong to call them merely trainees. I keep Liu alone for two reasons only: the committee's established practice is to credit the leader who conceived and directed the programme, and a trio would force out Buchwald or Hartwig. If the committee prefers Komor and Gaudelli and a single-part prize, I would rather hear that argued on evidence of who established what than on seniority. On Kondo and Nishida, I have not changed my view that the dates and the overlap in demonstrated chemistry must be checked before the committee excludes them, and I would not change the laureate list on this alone.

responses.point: Brzezinski pairs B032 (Gray and Winkler) with B058, calling B032 the part he can defend most firmly on evidence, and he acknowledges that it had weak opening support and overlaps with Marcus (1992) and the 1988 reaction-centre prize.
responses.response: I respect the quantitative case for distance and driving-force dependence of electron tunnelling in proteins, and I understand why you want to defer to colleagues because of your own research in this area. My concern is exactly the one you raised, that B032 refines a framework already honoured twice, and that the committee would have to say what new thing was established beyond Marcus theory. I find B030 easier to place because its mechanism is a design concept that gave a new capability, not a quantitative test of an established theory. Our shared Stockholm University affiliation does not affect this view, and I have noted it in my conflict statement.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, now pairs B058 with nanopore sensing (B050) as tools that write and read a single DNA strand, and he names Bayley and Akeson while he is open that Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz are excluded and that the chemistry content could be questioned.
responses.response: The write and read framing gives the two parts a thematic link that my own pairing lacks, and I count that in its favour. But the link makes the attribution problem worse, not better, because three founders are excluded, and you say yourself that the instrumentation and enzyme-motor engineering may outweigh the chemistry. In round 1 I suggested that one pioneer might be deceased. I could not verify that and withdraw it as an argument. The reason I keep B030 is the cleaner two-name credit and the closed question of reproducibility, not the thematic fit.

responses.point: Aili proposes ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B064) as a single-part prize for Cullis, Hope and Madden, and argues that it is lipid self-assembly and pKa-tuned design that enabled nucleic-acid medicines.
responses.response: The pKa-tuned lipid design and the link to patisiran and the mRNA vaccines make a real chemical case, and I did not rank B064 in my opening list for reasons of timing and credit, not because I doubt the science. The chair's question about separating Cullis, Hope and Madden from MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer remains the problem. Credit is spread across academic and industrial groups, the approved lipids were optimised in industry, and the 2023 Medicine prize overlaps on the same vaccines. For those reasons I do not move B064 into my configuration.

uncertainties: Whether Komor and Gaudelli, or Kondo and Nishida, must be credited for base editing, which would force a different configuration under the three-person limit.
Whether the committee accepts a two-part prize pairing a synthetic method with a chemical-biology tool, given that B030 had only two opening supporters.
Whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the 2020 CRISPR prize make B030 and B058 look like follow-on awards.
Whether the credit for Kosugi can be handled in the citation wording and background and not through a laureate slot.
statement.conflict_note: No recusal-level conflict. My field is electron crystallography and porous materials, and none of the shortlisted work comes from Stockholm University. I am a collegial colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski at Stockholm University, whose preferred B032 I do not support, so I note the tie for transparency only. I have no personal or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate.
